assessment: This manuscript examines how retinoic acid signaling controls the timing of neural crest production in avian embryos. The authors propose that local production of retinoic acid signaling activates the expression of BMP inhibitors in the dorsal neural tube. Disruption of BMP signaling results in the termination of neural crest migration and the establishment of the definite roof plate. In the absence of RA signaling cells in the dorsal neural tube continue to express neural crest markers well into the roof plate stage, and neural crest delamination is prolonged, but interestingly this does not prevent roof plate-mediated specification of dorsal interneurons.
